Faculty of Applied Sciences
05 October 2026
Developing a single AI system that can control different types of robots
Robots controlled by AI are developing at an ever-faster rate. In the near future, these robots could be used in society and in our daily lives. Normally, AI agents are trained to control a single specific robot and to be able to perform the wide variety of tasks of that robot. Researchers at Delft University of Technology are now developing an AI agent capable of controlling different types of robots. This AI system can use the knowledge it has gained from one robot to control other robots as well. The paper on this research project has been accepted to NeurIPS, the most competitive AI conference of the world.
30 September 2026
TU Delft launches new bachelor programme in Health and Technology
High school students making decisions about higher education will have a new option to consider this autumn. The BSc Health and Technology is a new TU Delft undergraduate programme which will educate graduates capable of designing and integrating the smart solutions and innovations needed to accelerate the healthcare transition.
21 September 2026
Measuring the Newtonian mechanics of roller coasters with your mobile phone
Where better to test Newton’s laws than at an amusement park? Acceleration, forces, energy and motion are present in all the rides. This article presents, for the first time, a complete reconstruction of the trajectory of rides by using data from motion sensors to calculate changes in position over time. This technique, known as odometry, enables a more in-depth mechanical analysis of amusement park rides.
03 September 2026
Five TU Delft researchers receive ERC Starting Grants
The European Research Council (ERC) has announced the ERC Starting Grants for young researchers. Five of them are scientists from TU Delft. This European grant of €1.5 million for a five-year research programme is intended to enable individual scientists to build their own teams and conduct groundbreaking research. A total of 33 scientists from Dutch universities and research institutions were awarded grants.
